8192 rather than 4096: a validation agent's reasoning `claim` runs to ~5.6K in
practice, and a claim dropped on length takes its whole `ReasoningStep` with
it. Deliberately NOT raised to the proof-body bound — this type is also the
member of a 50-entry `ReasoningSteps` list and of `ArtifactHeaders`, so its
bound multiplies into the worst-case response size.

projected body is read out of one `IssueArtifactContent`, itself bounded at
5 MiB, so no projection can exceed the size of the content it came from
whatever the member bounds permit. Keeping this one modest is about not
inflating a typical response, not about the ceiling.

traits.smithy.api#documentation: Ingests a customer-supplied security finding into an environment. Continuum validates the document synchronously against the required overlay fields for the declared format; invalid documents are rejected with a ValidationException. The maximum accepted document size is 256 KB. aws.iam#iamAction.documentation: Grants permission to start a code scan of an environment

traits.smithy.api#documentation:
Creates an explicit scan request for one environment. CP creates durable work before
any queue delivery occurs.

Retrying a request that succeeded, with the same clientToken on the same environment,
returns the original scan instead of starting another one. Token handling is not yet
atomic: requests with the same token that run at the same time, or a retry after a
request that failed partway through, can leave an additional scan, which may end in
the FAILED state with a message that it was superseded. Deleting the environment
makes its tokens unusable; a later request with one of them returns
ResourceNotFoundException.

Each environment can have a limited number of scans in progress at the same time.
Once that limit is enforced, a request that would exceed it returns
ServiceQuotaExceededException; wait for a scan to finish (ListCodeScans shows each
scan's status), then retry.
Environment to scan.

An optional token identifying one scan request for this environment. SDKs
generate a token when omitted. If a request reaches the service without a
token, the service generates one for that request, so each request without
a token starts a new scan. To retry a request after a lost response, supply
the same token on the same environment; once a request with that token has
succeeded, a retry returns the original scan. Concurrent requests with the
same token, or a retry after a request that failed partway through, can
leave an additional scan, which may end FAILED as superseded. A token is
bound to its scan for as long as the service retains the scan's build
record, with no shorter expiry. Deleting the environment makes the binding
inaccessible: a later request with the token returns
ResourceNotFoundException.

The scan run this request created, or the scan run a previous request with
the same clientToken already accepted.

Creates a new integration with an external source provider. Repeating an identical
request with the same clientToken returns the original integrationId, integrationArn,
and createdAt. Token records are retained for eight hours after success or terminal failure,
including after the integration is deleted; replaying a deleted integration's token
does not recreate it. An identical request with a retained terminal failure returns
the recorded error.

Reusing a token with different parameters returns ValidationException. A fresh token
starts a new create attempt; if the name is already owned by another integration,
ConflictException includes that integration's identifier. An attempt still in progress
may return ThrottlingException with retryAfterSeconds set to 1; retry with the same token
and identical parameters.

GitHub authorization codes are single use. Retry an unresolved attempt with its
original token and unchanged parameters first. If the service reports a terminal
failure, an expired attempt, or a successful token exchange whose integration could
not be saved, restart GitHub authorization with a fresh token and authorization code.
The service does not checkpoint provider results for recovery by another request.

current consumer needs the canonical complete, account-scoped environment inventory,

not needed by any current workflow. Adding speculative filters would require
unsupported access patterns and ambiguous semantics without reducing data returned
for existing consumers. If a concrete indexed query use case is introduced later, its
filter values must be bound to pagination tokens so a token cannot be replayed against
